facts.text: ds4 tensor parallelism runs the same graph on two ranks. Rank 0 (leader) runs the normal frontend session and mirrors every session sync and eval to rank 1 (worker) over a TCP control socket. Inside each decoded token the two ranks swap partial block outputs through a registered memory slab, by two-sided RDMA SEND/RECV when Thunderbolt RDMA works, otherwise by a full-duplex TCP exchange.

Launch order: start the worker first (it retries while the coordinator loads), then the coordinator. The worker command is `./ds4 --tensor-parallel --role worker --coordinator 10.99.0.2 9911 --transport rdma --ctx 8192` and the coordinator command is the same with `--role coordinator --listen 10.99.0.2 9911`. Do not pass `--layers`.
facts.note: privacy-ok (example address quoted from the cited source)

facts.text: The coordinator role can be `ds4`, `ds4-agent`, `ds4-server` or `ds4-bench`; the worker always runs `ds4`. A vision model needs the same `--vision FILE` on both. GLM MTP needs `--mtp` on both. V4.1 supports vision but not speculative decoding.

The leader listens and accepts one worker; the worker dials with retry; both then exchange an identity (GGUF byte size, model id, layer count, embedding width, vocabulary size, quant bits, context size and the gate schedule) and a mismatched pair aborts before any inference.
Each token exchanges two partials per layer, one after attention and one after the FFN (`DS4_TP_GATES_PER_LAYER = 2`), so a model with L layers makes 2L exchanges per decoded token.
Each partial is a float32 vector of `n_embd * 4` bytes and is "never quantized on the wire"; the activation-bit option belongs to pipeline mode only.

The slab holds `S = n_layer * 2` out vectors, `S` in vectors, `S` eight-byte sequence flags (written after each vector, so a flag proves its vector landed) and a 16-byte token slot sent leader to worker.

ds4 loads Apple's verbs library itself with `dlopen("/usr/lib/librdma.dylib")` and uses an unreliable-connection (UC) queue pair on macOS (reliable connection on Linux), MTU 1024, and global routing through the IPv4-mapped GID.
ds4 passes the index of the GID it selected as `sgid_index` in the RTR transition.
Device choice: ds4 looks at one verbs device per Thunderbolt port (`rdma_enN`) and picks the active one; `--rdma-device` and `--rdma-gid-index` override it.

Work split on two ranks: routed experts as one contiguous half per rank, attention heads split by `tp_head0 = rank * tp_heads`, the shared expert split into halves, prefill rows split into halves, dense weights replicated.
Speculative verify blocks (at most 5 rows, buffers up to 8) move all rows of a layer in one bulk RDMA transfer; prefill uses a bulk exchange with 2 MB TCP rounds as the fallback.
RDMA is skipped (TCP is used) when `n_embd * 4` bytes exceeds twice the RDMA maximum message size.
The TP wire protocol is at `DS4_TP_PROTOCOL_VERSION` 14 with magics `DS4T` and `DS4B`, and the comment on the 14th version says V4.1 CUDA workers "now return half-logit frames after successful work".
The librdma is loaded at runtime on purpose so builds and machines without RDMA still run.
Error text when no GID matches: "tp rdma: no IPv4-mapped GID on the active port; give the Thunderbolt interface its own IPv4 (e.g. sudo ifconfig en1 inet 10.99.0.2/30 alias) on both machines".

facts.text: Error text when no port is active: "no device with an active port ... is the peer up and rdma_ctl enabled on both machines?".
The source comment says the driver "only connects through the IPv4-mapped GID", which exists only when the member interface has its own IPv4 and "the bridge's address does not count".
A new UC queue pair can drop every send in one direction right after a working run or a role swap; ds4 detects this in its warm-up, recreates the pair and retries.
TP is exclusive with ds4's pipeline roles and layer slices: the validator rejects `--role` pipeline modes and `load_slice` with TP.
A TP option such as `--transport`, `--rdma-device` or `--rdma-gid-index` without `--tensor-parallel` and `--role` is an error.
Tunable environment variables: `DS4_TP_TIMEOUT_SEC` (default 300), `DS4_TP_GATE_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 750), `DS4_TP_DISABLE_VERIFY_WINDOW` and `DS4_TP_BIG_GATE_DEBUG`.

JACCL's `queue_pair_rtr` hard-codes `sgid_index = 1` while its `info()` accepts an IPv4-mapped GID at any index, so a GID table whose `::ffff:` entry is not at index 1 would be advertised from one index and routed from another. This could explain the errno 96 seen after IPv4 renumbering.

ds4 versus JACCL on GID handling. ds4 scans, uses the chosen index in RTR and fails early with a fix hint. JACCL scanned without failing until mlx PR 4191 added a similar hint, and still hard-codes index 1 at RTR.
Header comment versus code on what TP rejects: see aggregate-ssd-bandwidth-when-each-cluster-node-s.md.
Measured TP decode tok/s and per-gate latency for two-Mac RDMA are not published in the files read; the docs say only that gain depends on model, link and comparison setup.
Whether macOS 27 changes UC delivery, which would make ds4's one-direction-drop workaround unnecessary.
ds4 TP launch is worker first, then coordinator, with `--tensor-parallel --role ... --transport rdma` and the coordinator listening on a port such as 9911; `--layers` must not be passed.
ds4 TP exchanges two float32 partials per layer through a registered slab and never quantizes them on the wire.
ds4 TP's leader mirrors every session sync and eval to the worker over a TCP control socket so both run the identical graph sequence.
ds4 TP exchanges an engine identity at connect and aborts a mismatched pair before inference.
ds4 TP uses its own verbs calls through `/usr/lib/librdma.dylib`, a UC queue pair on macOS, MTU 1024 and the IPv4-mapped GID, not JACCL.
ds4 TP's sequence flag is written after its vector so a flag implies the vector landed.
ds4 TP's speculative verify blocks exchange up to 8 rows per layer in one bulk transfer.
ds4 TP's source says the bridge's IPv4 address does not count for the IPv4-mapped GID.
ds4 TP recreates a UC queue pair when a fresh pair drops all sends in one direction.
ds4 TP splits routed experts into contiguous halves, attention heads and shared-expert rows by rank, and replicates dense weights.
ds4's validator rejects TP combined with pipeline roles or layer slices.
ds4 TP is a 50/50 split with exactly one worker.
ds4's TP protocol version is 14.
A model with L layers costs 2L cross-machine exchanges per decoded token in ds4 TP, against about 2L all-sums in mlx-lm TP, with different transports.
JACCL's hard-coded `sgid_index = 1` at RTR may disagree with the GID index `info()` chose.
